It was a sharp two-way day: the Nasdaq fell 2.15% (-4.5% on the week, its worst since late June) as an eight-session chip losing streak, a software selloff and stress in AI-linked debt (CoreWeave -12%) hit semis, semicap, AI-infrastructure, AI-pivoting bitcoin miners and software names - so this pull's losers (Vicor, Supermicro, Ichor, Ultra Clean, ACM Research, MaxLinear, Viavi, DigitalOcean, Twilio, Okta, Five9, MARA, CleanSpark, Centrus) are mostly one sector-wide story, not 15 separate ones. Several of these names already had September writeups about earlier, opposite-direction moves; those are kept as 'Prior framing' under a dated UPDATE rather than overwritten. Supermicro is the main name with genuinely new company-specific news (an Oct 8-9 guilty plea in a server-diversion case that reopens a question the prior writeup called cleared). Gainers were almost entirely oil and gas: Brent settled near $110 (highest since May) and WTI near $101 on Iran's escalating Hormuz attacks and a large US crude draw, lifting E&Ps and midstream together. Most of those names had no company-specific catalyst and are marked as sector-beta reads; natural-gas futures actually fell that day, so gas-weighted names (Antero, Range) are marked divergent from their own commodity. Several volume outliers (Regions, Citizens, Alcoa, First Financial, Cohen & Steers) are earnings-driven; ten others (Schneider National, Sunstone, Urban Edge, DXP, Ormat, Avantor, Ecolab, Watts, Central Garden, Northern Trust) turned up no clean catalyst despite a genuine search - Oct 16 was a monthly options expiration, which commonly inflates volume, but that is stated as an unconfirmed explanation, not a sourced one.
